subject: English
passage: The Jurassic marine reptile Leedsichthys problematicus is known for having an exceptionally large body size. Until comprehensive tissue analysis was conducted in Argentina, paleontologists had been able to study only partial bone fragments from L. problematicus, though it was assumed that, like other large marine reptiles, the species was primarily a deep-water predator. Examining the tissue samples in 2017, Hirut Fantahun and her team determined that L. problematicus had fine gill structures, small teeth, and an unusually flexible jaw apparatus—characteristics that, combined with the creature's massive size, would have made hunting large prey inefficient and filter feeding in shallow waters highly effective. Based on these findings the team suggests that L. problematicus likely ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: hunted larger prey than did other marine reptile species that had exceptionally large body sizes.
choices.B: had larger teeth than other marine reptile species considered to have been effective filter feeders.
choices.C: fed on smaller organisms and spent more time in shallow waters than researchers previously thought.
choices.D: had a smaller body than researchers expected based on the earlier L. problematicus bone fragments.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of the Jurassic marine reptile Leedsichthys problematicus. The text first describes what paleontologists initially speculated to be true of L. problematicus based on observing only partial bone fragments rather than complete tissue samples—namely, that L. problematicus had an exceptionally large body and that, like other large marine reptiles, its main feeding strategy must have been deep-water predation. The text goes on to describe what researcher Hirut Fantahun and her team concluded based on studying comprehensive tissue samples of L. problematicus, which provided additional information that bone fragments alone could not. Fantahun and colleagues determined that L. problematicus had fine gill structures, small teeth, and an unusually flexible jaw apparatus, in addition to the large body size previously observed by paleontologists. Taken together, these characteristics would have made hunting large prey inefficient and filter feeding in shallow waters effective, which would make L. problematicus different from other marine reptiles that fed mainly through predation. Thus, Fantahun and colleagues suggest that previously held speculations of paleontologists are inaccurate: that instead of being primarily a deep-water predator, L. problematicus likely fed on smaller organisms and spent more time in shallow waters than researchers previously thought.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect because the tissue samples studied by Fantahun and colleagues revealed notably small teeth, and because no indication in the text is made that other marine reptiles were thought by paleontologists to be effective filter feeders. Therefore, Fantahun's team would not suggest that L. problematicus had larger teeth than other marine reptile species considered to have been effective filter feeders.
